pr_title: Several fixes around POSIX_SOURCE, remove global definitions of POSIX_SOURCE
pr_body:
Some cleanup around the selection of the API provided by the C library.
The main idea is to limit where the SOURCE selection is applied to much fewer files than before.

This PR includes some commits from #67040 so as to provide a complete solution. But it only includes those commits that are inline with the overall direction of this PR of removing all global definitions of these macros.

Background on the PR strategy differences: 
Currently #67040 cleans up only the global definitions done by picolibc, but sets newlibc to define those globally.
The current assumption in 67040 is that all functions listed in [the coding guidelines rules A.4 and A.5](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/contribute/coding_guidelines/index.html#rule-a-5-c-standard-library-usage-restrictions-in-zephyr-codebase) should be globally available, without needing to set any macro by the user file, even that some of those functions are not part of the C std library API but extensions. Unfortunately, this sets a requirement on the libC integration to ensure they are exposed. See https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/67040#issuecomment-1896476000.

Instead, this PR solves the global use of POSIX_SOURCE issue, while postponing deciding on and solving the libC integration topic ( https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/67040#discussion_r1462390520 ) 

-------

Notes about the checkpatch warnings:
* For the native port specific driver "bottoms", coding guidelines rules A.4/5 do not really apply as they intend to limit the C library use in the embedded code, while this is host code. So I would think those warnings should just be ignored. A PR to clarify the rule has been submitted ( #68004 )
* The warnings in subsys/shell/modules/devmem_service.c & subsys/net/lib/lwm2m/lwm2m_rw_cbor.c are violations by the original code, which are uncovered now.
  * #68002
  * #68003
* The warning in tests/bluetooth/uuid/src/test_bt_uuid_to_str.c & tests/benchmarks/footprints/src/libc.c are due to strnlen which is an exception to rule A.4, and therefore I think the checkpatch warning in this PR should be waived.

Sidenote: We can avoid all those check-patch warnings by defining these macros in cmake, but it does not feel nice to do so, just because of checkpatch.

----

Fixes #66921

issue_context.title: arch: posix: _POSIX_C_SOURCE declaration conflicts with the rest of the system
issue_context.body: **Describe the bug** Picolibc and arch/posix both globally define a number of symbols reserved by IEEE-1003.1-2017 (and many earlier versions of the standard) such as `_POSIX_C_SOURCE`, `_XOPEN_SOURCE` for all Zephyr builds on that architecture, even Zephyr builds which do not explicitly want or use `CONFIG_POSIX_API=y` or any POSIX [subprofiling options](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/services/portability/posix/option_groups/index.html). This is a bit of an issue, because a) it means virtually every platform is in violation of [Rules A.4 and A.5 of the Coding Guidelines](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/66921) since * ~2018 for arch/posix * ~2020 (based on commit date) for lib/libc/picolibc b) since the compile definitions are hard-coded and global, they prevent applications from defining (correct, standard) application conformance levels without risking a compiler error It seems to only be an issue since `native_sim` has facilitated running applications that enable features defined by Zephyr's POSIX API for approximately 6 months. Please also mention any information which could help others to understand the problem you're facing: - What target platform are you using? all - What have you tried to diagnose or workaround this issue? PRs, etc - Is this a regression? No **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: Attempt to build any application conforming to the IEEE 1003.1-1-2017 standard with either up-to-date `_POSIX_C_SOURCE` (200809L) or up-to-date `_XOPEN_SOURCE` (700). (note: 1. ```shell echo -e "#define _POSIX_C_SOURCE 200809L\n#define _XOPEN_SOURCE 700" \ | cat - samples/hello_world/src/main.c > /tmp/foo.c mv /tmp/foo.c samples/hello_world/src/main.c ``` 2. `west build -b native_sim_64 samples/hello_world` 2. Observe errors. **Expected behavior** Ideally the internal compiler definitions used for `ARCH_POSIX` and Picolibc would not spill out and affect the rest of the build. POSIX application conformance macros should only be local compile definitions, and not global compile definitions. **Impact** Originally this had not been noticed until after `native_sim` was added, since it was not supported to enable `CONFIG_POSIX_API` and `CONFIG_ARCH_POSIX` together for many years. They were mutually exclusive due to architectural issues. However, now that POSIX_API is ramping up significantly and nearing feature-completion, we are seeing more frequent conflicts. Originally, this was only an issue on `native_sim` and `native_sim_64`, but now seems to be affecting all platforms, since it is a bit of a showstopper for the [POSIX Roadmap for LTSv3](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/51211). **Logs and console output** ```shell src/main.c.obj -MF CMakeFiles/app.dir/src/main.c.obj.d -o CMakeFiles/app.dir/src/main.c.obj -c /tmp/zephyrproject/zephyr/samples/hello_world/src/main.c /tmp/zephyrproject/zephyr/samples/hello_world/src/main.c:1: error: "_POSIX_C_SOURCE" redefined [-Werror] 1 | #define _POSIX_C_SOURCE 200809L | : note: this is the location of the previous definition /tmp/zephyrproject/zephyr/samples/hello_world/src/main.c:2: error: "_XOPEN_SOURCE" redefined [-Werror] 2 | #define _XOPEN_SOURCE 700 ``` **Environment (please complete the following information):** - OS: Linux - Toolchain: Zephyr SDK v0.16.4 - Commit: 87d056bd31b14b680e6f011134c7ce433c4462f6 **Additional context** Related PRs (IIRC, Newlib and Picolibc might also have issues here) https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/67040
comments: It seems that this issue is also not avoided by using `zephyr_library_compile_definitions()`. There was a hypothesis that this would limit compile definitions to the library being built, but as of now, it's quite easy to demonstrate broken on `main`. The same issue exists if `zephyr_compile_definitions()` are used in both locations. ```diff diff --git a/arch/posix/CMakeLists.txt b/arch/posix/CMakeLists.txt index dc83cecc61..8b7bd8ffe6 100644 --- a/arch/posix/CMakeLists.txt +++ b/arch/posix/CMakeLists.txt @@ -133,7 +133,7 @@ if (CONFIG_GPROF) target_link_options(native_simulator INTERFACE "-pg") endif() -zephyr_compile_definitions(_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809 _XOPEN_SOURCE=600 _XOPEN_SOURCE_EXTENDED) +zephyr_library_compile_definitions(_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809 _XOPEN_SOURCE=600 _XOPEN_SOURCE_EXTENDED) if (CONFIG_NATIVE_APPLICATION) zephyr_ld_options( diff --git a/lib/posix/CMakeLists.txt b/lib/posix/CMakeLists.txt index c6b3a88aea..d1c2bc391f 100644 --- a/lib/posix/CMakeLists.txt +++ b/lib/posix/CMakeLists.txt @@ -35,6 +35,7 @@ if(CONFIG_POSIX_API OR CONFIG_PTHREAD_IPC OR CONFIG_POSIX_CLOCK OR endif() zephyr_library() +zephyr_library_compile_definitions(_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L _XOPEN_SOURCE=700) ``` ```shell west build -p auto -b native_sim_64 -t run tests/posix/common/ ```

> It seems that this issue is also not avoided by using `zephyr_library_compile_definitions()`. There was a hypothesis that this would limit compile definitions to the library being built, but as of now, it's quite easy to demonstrate broken on `main`.

`zephyr_library_compile_definitions()` works fine. You need to
a) Also change the line setting those macros for PICOLIBC
b) For the posix arch cmake, to set it when you are in the scope of the library, not the whole Zephyr scope/not when  `ZEPHYR_CURRENT_LIBRARY` is the whole Zephyr.
 
```diff
diff --git a/arch/posix/CMakeLists.txt b/arch/posix/CMakeLists.txt
index dc83cecc61..7001e54e75 100644
--- a/arch/posix/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/arch/posix/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -133,8 +133,6 @@ if (CONFIG_GPROF)

 endif()
 
-zephyr_compile_definitions(_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809 _XOPEN_SOURCE=600 _XOPEN_SOURCE_EXTENDED)
-
 if (CONFIG_NATIVE_APPLICATION)
   zephyr_ld_options(
     -ldl
diff --git a/arch/posix/core/CMakeLists.txt b/arch/posix/core/CMakeLists.txt
index 3cf83c9fdd..06640d0675 100644
--- a/arch/posix/core/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/arch/posix/core/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -1,6 +1,7 @@
 # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 
 zephyr_library()
+zephyr_library_compile_definitions(_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809 _XOPEN_SOURCE=600 _XOPEN_SOURCE_EXTENDED)
 zephyr_library_compile_definitions(NO_POSIX_CHEATS)
 zephyr_library_sources(
        cpuhalt.c
diff --git a/lib/libc/picolibc/CMakeLists.txt b/lib/libc/picolibc/CMakeLists.txt
index 232e4ba8fc..5811a9cefa 100644
--- a/lib/libc/picolibc/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/lib/libc/picolibc/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -12,7 +12,7 @@ if(NOT CONFIG_PICOLIBC_USE_MODULE)
   # Use picolibc provided with the toolchain
 
   zephyr_compile_options(--specs=picolibc.specs)
-  zephyr_compile_definitions(_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809)
+  zephyr_library_compile_definitions(_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809)
   zephyr_libc_link_libraries(--specs=picolibc.specs c -lgcc)
   if(CONFIG_PICOLIBC_IO_FLOAT)
     zephyr_compile_definitions(PICOLIBC_DOUBLE_PRINTF_SCANF)
diff --git a/lib/posix/CMakeLists.txt b/lib/posix/CMakeLists.txt
index c6b3a88aea..d1c2bc391f 100644
--- a/lib/posix/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/lib/posix/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -35,6 +35,7 @@ if(CONFIG_POSIX_API OR CONFIG_PTHREAD_IPC OR CONFIG_POSIX_CLOCK OR
 endif()
 
 zephyr_library()
+zephyr_library_compile_definitions(_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L _XOPEN_SOURCE=700)
 add_subdirectory_ifdef(CONFIG_GETOPT getopt)
 zephyr_library_sources_ifdef(CONFIG_EVENTFD eventfd.c)
 zephyr_library_sources_ifdef(CONFIG_FNMATCH fnmatch.c)
```

Removing the regression label as this has been the case since 2017. So it is not something that was working that broke due to some recent commit.

And clarifying that the issue is that if somebody wants to set _POSIX_C_SOURCE to 200809L they find themselves forced to set it to _POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809. So the assessment would be at an annoyance level, as the worst case is that somebody has some source setting this macro, and they need to either undef _POSIX_C_SOURCE first, or not set it in their code, or set it to the same value.
=> removing the "priority: high" label as that label is meant for bugs which break the majority of development in tree.

Something in the tree being done in a simple way which needs changing to support a new feature being developed, is not a bug that blocks new development, it is simply something that needs to be changed to develop that new feature.

Just setting this to medium (it was high), because it's affecting every platform, causes violations of [rules A.4 and A.5](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/contribute/coding_guidelines/index.html) for just about every platform, and the release is coming up.

I would prefer to make this `priority: high` (and it was originally set to that 1 month ago).

review_comments: I think this workaround is fine, but we should probably switch to the ISO C `gmtime_s()` here, eventually.
I would very much have that handled in a separate discussion as to allow this fix to progress.

As a harmless safety.
A user may define this globally, another library may due to legacy or by mistake.
It is safe to undef macros even if they were never defined.
Given that we are here due to conflicts in this area, and that some feel strongly about defining this kind of macro globally, and that Zephyr as an OS is built quite monotonically with the app it seemed reasonable to play safe.
Wouldn't you want to add them on your PR? :)
